prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a workshop floor receding downward to ~1.5–2.0 m below the downward-looking camera wearer, a large blue tool cabinet on the left to center at ~0.4–1.2 m, a car wheel/tire at ~0.6–1.0 m in front and below, and a second person partly visible on the far left at ~1.0–1.5 m. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer approaches and turns slightly right toward the tool cabinet as they roll the wheel forward and lean it against the cabinet's lower right side (~0.2 m separation), while the camera wearer's left arm rises in frames 4–5 to rest on the top edge of the cabinet within ~0.3–0.5 m (well within arm's reach, as is the tire in frames 1–3) and partially occludes the cabinet's left side. The second person on the left is mostly out of view (only legs in frame 1, head/shoulder in frame 3, and left arm/torso in frame 5 facing roughly parallel to the cabinet and not looking at the camera wearer) and stands ~0.5–1.0 m to the left of the cabinet. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground raised left arm and the tall vertical cabinet planes from the deeper concrete floor and background clutter. However, the depth map is unreliable in frames 3–5 where the upper-left cabinet corner and the wearer's upper sleeve saturate to uniform white and where background workshop objects above and behind the cabinet drop out into flat black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the foreground limbs of the camera wearer (at ~0.2–0.8 m below and in front), the second person on the far left (~1.0–1.5 m away and ~0.5–1.0 m left of the cabinet), and the car wheel (~0.6–1.2 m in front and below), while omitting the large blue tool cabinet (~0.4–1.2 m away) and concrete floor (~1.5–2.0 m below) entirely into the black background. In frames 1–3, both of the camera wearer's arms reach down within arm's reach (~0.4–0.8 m) to hold and position the wheel against the lower right side of the unsegmented cabinet, before the right arm drops out of view and the left arm lifts up to rest on the cabinet's top left in frame 4 and disappears in frame 5. The second person on the far left—partially occluded by the frame border and facing away/sideways rather than toward the camera wearer—is segmented only in frame 1 (legs/lower torso) and missed in frames 3 and 5 when their arm and torso reappear near the cabinet's left side within arm's reach of the cabinet tray. While the masks clearly delineate the silhouette boundaries of the wearer's arms and the circular wheel rim against the floor and cabinet where lighting and shadows merge in RGB, the map is highly unreliable in class labels and temporal consistency. Specifically, it mislabels tools in the top-left corner of frame 1 as 'scissors', the tire in frame 1 as 'remote'/'cell phone', and the wheel rim in frames 4–5 as a 'clock', while fragmenting the wearer's arms and legs into multiple separate 'person' instances and missing the wearer's left arm and second person completely in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 3D-projected hand landmarks (magenta) of the camera wearer in frames 1–3 and the left arm and hand skeleton (yellow and magenta) of the second person on the far left in frame 5, against a black background that omits the tool cabinet (~0.4–1.2 m), wheel (~0.6–1.2 m), and floor (~1.5–2.0 m). In frames 1–3, the camera wearer's left and right hands are ~0.3–0.4 m apart and ~0.5–0.8 m in front of and below the viewpoint—within direct arm's reach as they grip the tire treads and rotate rightward to lean the wheel against the cabinet's lower face—before both hands move out of view or become occluded in frames 4–5 as the wearer approaches the cabinet. In frame 5, the second person stands ~1.0–1.2 m to the left of the camera wearer and ~0.5 m left of the cabinet, with their torso partially out of frame, facing parallel to the cabinet rather than looking at the camera wearer, and their left elbow bent with the forearm raised upward within arm's reach of the cabinet's side shelf. The skeleton map reveals the precise finger articulation of the wearer's grip on the dark tire in frames 1–3 and isolates the second person's raised left arm and hand posture in frame 5 despite motion blur and clutter in the RGB image. However, it is unreliable wherever body parts are heavily foreshortened or truncated by the egocentric frame boundary, failing to connect the wearer's hands to a body skeleton in frames 1–3, missing the wearer's raised left arm in frame 4, and failing to detect the second person's legs in frame 1 or partial body in frame 3.
